findings.claim: San Anselmo qualifies as an owner-confirmed construction/current-solar example; public emergency readiness remains unverified. It was not selected as an optimal East Bay location.

Hayward announced routine library-hour reductions for municipal budget savings effective January 1 2026. Current schedule closes both branches Sunday/Monday; ordinary meetings must be within library hours and reserved at least 30 days ahead.
findings.freshness: Late discovery; no claim of new September change

findings.claim: A library expected to absorb heat/communications demand can lose staffed opening capacity under the same broader fiscal stress affecting other services; ownership and building capital do not establish usable public reserve.
findings.threshold: Reduced hours overlap actual need and alternative sites cannot absorb demand
buffers: Independent partner site with agreed access
findings.confirm: Published or observed service gap under heat/outage coincident with staffing limits
findings.falsify: Funded and successfully exercised activation at appropriate hours, with sufficient alternative capacity

findings.claim: OakCLT documents an acquired mixed-use community asset with nonprofit storefronts and garden, demonstrating a local land-stewardship path beyond short room bookings.
findings.freshness: Historical model newly examined; no available property inferred

findings.claim: No shortlisted location has a verified allocation to this project, a measured emergency power/water floor, or a agreed surge staffing plan.

commons_proposal.name: Durably controlled minimum commons
commons_proposal.essential_function: Accessible everyday learning, information and mutual support, with a small independently operable critical room
tenure_options: Community land trust or cooperative acquisition
Multiyear operating agreement at existing institution with keys, storage, hours, hosting/alteration rights and clear termination responsibilities
first_steps: Choose an existing willing institution only after agreement; published listing is not consent
Define one accessible room, secure storage, sanitation, staffing and protected host service floor
Measure actual critical electrical loads and water needs; distinguish daily utility from tested outage endurance
Fund rotating staple food/procurement and replenishment; treat rescued surplus as additional supply
Name a second node after comparing utility, route, funding and staffing dependencies
Run a small observed service drill and record usable hours rather than installed nameplate capacity
success_measures: Secure access and actual usable opening hours
commons_proposal.donor_guardrail: Preserve ordinary users, paid staff, maintenance obligations and each partner protected reserve. No assumed capacity or rights in another organization.

peer_exchange.sent: Hayward budget/hour contraction can erode expected fallback. Room bookings do not confer outage access.
peer_exchange.received: Food bank supply mix includes purchasing/government/recovered food; protect rotating meal floor plus water/energy/staff/transport. Different donor names can share suppliers and routes.

RYSE title and battery commissioning unverified

review_recommendations: Admit Hayward service/fiscal fact as late discovery, keep causal heat-service link conditional
Retain San Anselmo as completion example; do not upgrade to verified usable surge reserve
Add control/access rights, operating budget, staffing and replenishment to commons readiness record
Do not conflate public ownership with autonomous community control or treat named nodes as available property
